input.purpose: Measure the Lab served air volume V_lab from the CO2 response to a scrubber speed change.
hypotheses: The closed Lab hatch makes /habitat/lab a single well-mixed zone for the fit; residual exchange through the closed hatch is not measured and is not assumed to be zero.
The one Lab occupant remains present at steady activity for both phases, so occupant CO2 generation is approximately steady.
The scrubber effective flow follows its accepted speed command and its registered full-speed flow and single-pass removal efficiency apply in place.
A 30-minute rise and 30-minute decay provide enough response to fit the equilibrium-offset exponential within the signed 60-minute test envelope.

monitoring.reason: The reduced-flow phase raises the CO2 breathed by the Lab occupant; stop on an out-of-band or lost signal.

steps.why: Hold the Lab as one zone and reduce effective flow so CO2 rises several hundred ppm above sensor noise; record Lab and Hab-B CO2, accepted command, occupancy, and speed at one-minute intervals.
Keep all other conditions fixed, restore full speed, and record the decay at one-minute intervals; fit C(t)=C_eq+(C_0-C_eq) exp(-t/tau), then calculate V_lab=Qe*tau.

abort.when: Lab CO2 is at or above 3000 ppm.
The scrubber refuses either commanded speed.
Scrubber battery state of charge is under 35 percent.
CDR is outside 45-120 bpm, monitoring is lost, or any additional person enters the Lab.

expected.ifHypothesesHold: With the hatch closed and CDR continuously present at steady activity, Lab CO2 rises during the 30 percent phase and then decays smoothly toward a nonzero equilibrium at 100 percent. A fit of the full-speed segment to the equilibrium-offset exponential yields tau; registered effective flow Qe times tau yields V_lab in m3.
expected.openingExchangeCheck: Hab-B CO2 should not track the Lab transient strongly. Correlated Lab and Hab-B changes indicate material exchange through the closed hatch and invalidate the one-zone interpretation unless exchange is modeled.
expected.sourceStabilityCheck: Any entry, exit, or activity change invalidates the steady-source curve; abort on an additional Lab occupant and flag visible activity changes during review.
expected.deviceCheck: A refused command, speed telemetry inconsistent with the requested plateau, or a curve that does not reverse from rise to decay shows the pump hypothesis does not hold; do not report V_lab from that run.
expected.fitAcceptance: Compare the recorded curve with the prewritten exponential prediction and report residuals and uncertainty; do not force a fit toward zero or outdoor concentration.
